title: Megan’s program v2
author: Adam Rowland
desc:
Progression Rules & Guidelines

General Principles
	•	Form first, load second. Prioritize technique over heavier weight.

	•	Stop 2–3 reps before failure; joint/back pain is not normal.

	•	Progress one variable at a time: increase reps → pause/tempo → load.

	•	Pain ≠ progress. Regress immediately if discomfort occurs.

	•	Deload if joints feel stressed, fatigue persists, or progress stalls.

Warm-Up
	•	5–10 min light cardio if desired.
	•	Dynamic mobility: arm circles, leg swings (front-back, side-side).
	•	Activation sets: light sets of heavy lifts (Hip thrust, Leg press, KB swing) before working sets.

Cool-Down / Stretching
	•	Stretch muscles worked that day: glutes, hamstrings, quads, calves, hip flexors, chest, back.
	•	Stretch gently, hold 15–30 sec per muscle group.
	•	Avoid over-stretching joints if hypermobile.

ex.note: Lie on back, band above knees, feet hip-width, heels under knees. Push hips up, squeeze glutes, lower slowly. Activates glutes & stabilizes hips. 2 or 3 sets
Use the machine or barbell. Hinge at the hips and slow going down, be in control of the weight. Squeeze at the top and hold for a second. Do a warmup set using 50% of the weight.
Tighten core, bend at the hips and visualise pushing them as far back as possible whilst sliding the bar down until just past your knees. Stand up straight and sqeeze.
Put your feet slightly high and at shoulder width to bias the glutes. Go as deep as your feel comfortable, ideally until your knees are bent at 90 degrees. Don’t lock out.
Slow eccentric. Count 3 seconds when lowering the weight.

Remember how I showed you, keep whole body still, don’t move hips. Lock your ankle and point to slightly outward and swing leg diagonally feeling a squeeze at the top of glute. Bring the leg down slow
Amazing for posture. Set cable at face height. Grab rope, pull toward face, elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades. Keep core tight, back straight. Use light weight, controlled motion
Sit or stand, hold kettlebell, pass it in a circle around your torso. Keep core tight, spine neutral. Builds obliques & rotational stability. 6-10 in each direction
Get maximum chest activation by keeping shoulder blades retracted (push them back and down).
Back straight,leaning back slightly when pulling down. visualise pulling your elbows down until they’re tucked into your side and squeezing shoulder blades down. try a neutral grip attachment.
Back straight, tight core. Pull until your elbows are by your hips and then slowly extend letting your shoulders feel the stretch.
Optional, Biceps and triceps get worked well in the earlier exercises, do these if you have the time or feel extra motivated.
